input.sha256_scope: The committed classic-v1-benchmark-page/input.png, which one of the three cases uses. The other two are deterministic synthetic pages generated by formula on both sides.
input.provenance: No new input pixels. One case reuses an already-committed fixture PNG; the other two are generated by a closed-form expression reproduced identically in the capture tool and the Rust test.

limitations: One case, synthetic-1, is recorded as NOT reproduced exactly: reproduced_exactly is false. The cubic resize diverges from OpenCV's fixed-point path by roughly one pixel in eighty thousand at page scale, and the test bounds that divergence rather than hiding it. This is a known open defect, not a tolerance.

Three pages, only one of them a real composed document, and it yields a single detection above 0.5. Nothing here shows the model finds a realistic document's layout; it shows this port feeds it the same tensor and decodes its answer the same way.
The preprocessing is transcribed from the pinned PaddleX 3.7.2 source, not imported. An upstream change to those operators would not be detected here.
The model's raw detections are recorded rather than reproduced offline. The committed fixture checks the input tensor and the decode; running the model needs the provisioned artifact.
No NMS. PaddleX exposes layout_nms as an option and this fixture captures it off, which is the default.
